prompt: jq |= update-assignment right-hand side outputs empty
answer:
In `jq`, `|=` runs the RHS filter against the current value of the LHS. If that filter produces no value—`empty`—the LHS path is deleted. This is the documented behavior for current jq versions. ([jq manual](https://manpages.debian.org/trixie/jq/jq.1.en.html))

```sh
jq -cn '{a:{b:{c:1,d:2}}} |
  .a.b.c |= select(. != 1)'
```

Output:

```json
{"a":{"b":{"d":2}}}
```

If you want to keep the existing value, make the RHS output `.` instead of `empty`:

```jq
.foo |= if condition then new_value else . end
```

Also, if the RHS produces multiple values, current jq uses only the first; jq 1.5 and earlier used the last.
